sections.h2: Who mails the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
The Town of East Hampton Receiver of Taxes prepares and mails the bills. The Assessor's Office sets the assessed values behind them. The receiver's office handles more than 24,000 bills and passes the money on to Suffolk County, the general town fund, nine fire and fire protection districts, six school districts with five associated libraries and one museum district, five lighting districts, five road improvement and water connection districts, and special use districts. That mix is why two houses a few streets apart can carry different totals: the bill depends on which fire, school, lighting and road districts cover the parcel.

The town takes in the village of East Hampton, the hamlets of Montauk, Amagansett, Wainscott, Springs, Northwest Harbor and Napeague, and part of the village of Sag Harbor. The Assessor's Office produces the yearly assessment roll, keeps ownership records and exemption files, and maintains district maps that follow the official Suffolk County tax maps. Bills can be viewed and printed on the official Tax Receiver page even after collection closes.

sections.h2: Payment dates and what changes after May 31
sections.html:
Taxes are payable to the town receiver from December 1 through May 31, in two halves. January 10 ends the interest-free period for the first installment, after which 1% a month accrues. The second installment carries no interest through the end of May. Bills go out by mid-December.

Collection ends each year on June 1, and the online and phone payment systems close. From then on every payment, with penalties and interest, goes to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, phone 631-852-3000. Include your tax map number and contact details, and consider certified mail for proof of mailing.

  • After May 31 the Comptroller adds a 5% penalty plus interest at 1% per month counted from February 1, applied to the tax plus penalty.
  • Taxes still unpaid on August 31 pick up a tax sale advertising fee.
  • Partial payments of at least $200 are accepted, and penalty and interest then run on the unpaid balance only.
  • Mailed payments count by the postmark date. A metered postmark does not count.

If a bill never reaches you, the Comptroller still holds the owner liable for penalties and interest, so ask the receiver for a duplicate as soon as you notice the gap.

File a complaint on form RP-524 with the town assessor during the grievance period, which runs from May 1 through Grievance Day on the third Tuesday in May. In 2027 that is May 18. The yearly cycle looks like this:

DateWhat happens
July 1 of the prior yearValuation date
March 1Taxable status date; new exemption applications and renewals are due
May 1Tentative roll opens for public viewing and the grievance period starts
July 1Final roll for the current year
30 days after the final roll closesDeadline for a Suffolk small claims assessment review (SCAR)

The town does not accept grievance or exemption applications by email or fax. For proof that your grievance arrived, send it return receipt. The forms page links a guide to disputing an assessment.

East Hampton is mostly owner-occupied, with about 77.8 percent of homes lived in by their owners. The estimated population in 2025 was 29,400, and the median home value is $1,178,500. At that level even a small difference in assessed value moves the tax bill noticeably, which is one reason a grievance can pay off for an owner whose assessment looks high against recent nearby sales.

sections.h2: Does STAR still lower school tax?
sections.html:
Yes, through the STAR credit. The credit arrives as a check or direct deposit that you use toward school taxes. The older exemption on the bill continues only for people who have received it since 2015 on the same primary residence, and it is closed to new homeowners. New Basic and Enhanced STAR applicants register with the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance.

The Basic credit has an income limit of $500,000, and Enhanced STAR, for owners aged 65 and over, requires income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-2027 school year. STAR applies to school district taxes only. To qualify for a credit in a given year, you must own the property and live in it as your primary residence as of July 1 of that year. A buyer who closes after that date registers for the following year.

sections.h2: What if tax is still open when I sell?
sections.html:
A delinquent balance stays attached to the parcel, so it has to be paid or settled around the time title transfers. If taxes are still unpaid at the tax lien sale, usually held in December, the Comptroller sells a lien to Suffolk County to cover the delinquent tax for that year. The owner or anyone with an interest can redeem within twelve months of the sale date. A one, two or three-family residence gets thirty-six months. If the redemption period lapses, the county issues a tax deed, and an application to redeem after that goes to the Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate.

  1. Pull your current bill from the receiver's portal to see what is paid for the year.
  2. If anything from an earlier year is open, call the Comptroller at 631-852-3000 for a payoff figure that includes penalty and interest.
  3. Hand that figure to your closing attorney or title agent so the balance is settled at the closing table.
  4. Tell the buyer to contact the receiver for a current bill, since new owners are advised to do exactly that.

In an as-is sale the payoff is one more item on the closing statement. The receiver and the Comptroller are the two offices that can supply it.

faqs.q: When is the first half of East Hampton property tax due?
faqs.a: January 10 is the last interest-free day for the first installment. From January 11 the unpaid half grows by 1% each month. The second installment stays interest-free until the end of May.

faqs.q: Where do I pay East Hampton tax after May 31?
faqs.a: To the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, phone 631-852-3000. The town's online and phone systems close once collection ends, so include your tax map number and use certified mail if you pay by post.

faqs.q: Will the town waive the penalty if I never received my bill?
faqs.a: No. The taxpayer is responsible for tax on property they own, and a bill that never arrived does not remove penalties or interest. Ask the receiver for a duplicate bill as soon as you notice it is missing.

faqs.q: When must an East Hampton grievance be filed?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. Filing opens May 1 with the tentative roll. Email and fax filings are refused.

faqs.q: Can I sell my East Hampton house while the county holds a tax lien on it?
faqs.a: Yes, once the lien is settled at or before the closing. Suffolk lets an owner redeem within twelve months of the lien sale, or thirty-six months for a one to three family home. Get the payoff from the Comptroller and pass it to whoever runs your closing.
